question: By what means, addressed to the fair-faced one, is a result said to be attained through both hearing and mere knowledge?
premises: An address is made to the fair-faced one.
A means is given as mere knowledge.
That means is also described as what has been heard.
The two are joined by ca as a single instrumental means.
inference: By this means—mere knowledge that has been heard—something is attained, O fair-faced one.
uncertainties: The result attained is not stated in this verse.
plain_english: By this mere knowledge, which has been heard, O fair-faced one.
